title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\varphi^n\rfloor$
summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio and let $R_n=\{\lfloor k\varphi^n\rfloor : k\ge 1\}$ be the $n$-th row of the array $T(n,k)=\lfloor k\varphi^n\rfloor$ (OEIS A128440). In 2022 Kimberling conjectured that the rows $R_{2n-1}$ and $R_{2n}$ are disjoint, and that after the two rows are merged and each entry is replaced by its rank, they become the lower and upper Wythoff sequences. He also conjectured (OEIS A358359) that if $a(N)$ is the number of rows containing $N$, then every positive integer occurs infinitely often among the values of $a$. We show that the first two conjectures follow…
